imagePrompt: Create one 1536 x 1024 pixel painted scene sheet, EXACTLY TWO COLUMNS BY THREE ROWS, six equal-width WIDE cinematic panels in row-major order 0 to 5. Each column is 768 pixels; rows are approximately 341, 341 and 342 pixels high. Hard straight cell edges; no gutters, no panel labels, no numbers, no captions, no typography, no readable lettering, no logos. Every cell is its own complete environment, never a sprite or a cutout. Use the polished watercolor and fine ink on textured cream paper style of Enough: warm directional light, deep teal and umber shadows, restrained paper grain, expressive natural faces, subtle imperfect painted edges. Human anatomy is believable, heads naturally sized; shoulders, elbows, wrists, hands, hips and knees belong to one continuous body. Seat hips on the actual seat, feet on the same floor, fingers visibly holding their actual objects; no disembodied hands, duplicated limbs, floating props or pasted-on heads. Keep important faces, hands, contact points and grounded figures within each wide panel with safe margins. Maintain the same identities, clothing, figure scale, prop design and spatial continuity across all six scenes. Anonymous original visual casting only, not likenesses of credited storytellers. This is a dramatic storyboard adaptation, not a claim that imagined symbols or staged details are verified events. Story: One Voice. Palette accents: #D3E0E1, #3E596B, #F0B96B. Identity continuity: PASSENGER: The same adult man with tan skin, short dark brown hair, muted teal-blue shirt and slate trousers, seated on a subway bench, initially uncertain and later willing to join. WOMAN: The same adult woman with deeper brown skin, long dark hair, muted coral blouse and slate skirt; she begins the wordless sound tentatively, without becoming a stage singer. PERSON 3: The same third adult passenger with lighter warm brown skin, short dark hair, muted lavender top and slate trousers; visibly distinct from the first man and woman, joins later and tentatively. TOP LEFT (frame 0): An ordinary subway carriage with three distinct passengers seated at believable distances on a bench, feet on the shared floor, hands holding their own bags or resting on knees. Above the aisle hangs one oversized dark jagged empty speech-shape suggesting hostile pressure, with no hateful wording and no depicted attacker. The man looks sideways uneasily, the woman keeps her gaze low and the third person avoids eye contact. Ordinary rails and windows keep the situation grounded. TOP RIGHT (frame 1): The woman sits more upright and places one hand softly on her own upper chest, fingers flat against fabric while the other remains on her lap. Her face is unsure, lips slightly parted as she looks toward the nearby man, who listens without instructing her. The third passenger still looks down. Keep the same carriage bench, bags and rail positions. The jagged pressure shape remains above, not touching anyone or becoming an actual creature. MIDDLE LEFT (frame 2): The woman begins a small hum with relaxed closed lips and a visible gentle exhale in her posture, one hand now resting low on her knee. A single warm ochre curved note-like mark emerges near her face, an abstract unlettered sound symbol. The nearby man begins to lift his eyes while the third passenger remains hesitant. Her body stays ordinarily seated, with no spotlight, microphone, performing stage pose or musical fantasy set. MIDDLE RIGHT (frame 3): The man has turned naturally toward the woman, head lifted and mouth softening in recognition. She meets his glance and keeps the tiny hum. A second restrained curved mark appears near him, separated from hers by real carriage air. Their hands rest on their own laps and their bodies remain distinct, not leaning into a romantic tableau. The third passenger watches with tentative interest. The threatening shape is still visible but less central. BOTTOM LEFT (frame 4): The third passenger lifts their face and begins a shy hum, mouth only slightly open and hands releasing a tight grip on their own bag. The first two passengers continue quietly. Three separate small ochre sound marks are linked by a thin restrained curve above their individual shoulders, never binding bodies together. The jagged dark shape has become smaller and more distant in the carriage. Keep all three faces natural, tentative and different. BOTTOM RIGHT (frame 5): A wider view holds the same three ordinary passengers and the warm line of a few unlettered sound marks among them, while the dark threatening shape has receded to a small edge trace. They remain seated with real bag contacts and grounded feet, exchanging modest looks of solidarity rather than huge grins. The subway is still a subway, with no transformed audience, arrested villain or concert ending. Distinct people share a little more courage. Story-specific safeguards: No hateful wording or slurs in the image. No invented confrontation, arrest or identified threatening person. Use only an original or licensed melody; do not reproduce an identifiable song or imply cleared musical rights. The existing caption Hmm... is preserved verbatim; sound symbols are abstract, not painted lettering.
